what: Symptom: Conformal quantile returns the maximum nonconformity score or upper bound is uninformative
title: Getting Help and Troubleshooting
text: Cause (Mathematical Degeneracy): held-calibration set small requested miscoverage level α\alpha. Conformal prediction requires: Ncal≥⌈1−αα⌉N_{\text{cal}} \ge \left\lceil \frac{1 - \alpha}{\alpha} \right\rceil example, requesting 99% interval (α=0.01\alpha = 0.01) Ncal=40N_{\text{cal}} = 40 mathematically calibrate 99% empirical quantile, highest empirical quantile available 1−1/(Ncal+1)=97.6%1 - 1/(N_{\text{cal}} + 1) = 97.6\%. Fix: Either increase calibration partition size via split (e.g. split = 0.5 instead 0.8), choose α\alpha commensurate sample size (e.g. α=0.05\alpha = 0.05 0.100.10).

text: scp_areal() constructs distribution-free prediction intervals areal units (polygons, counties, grid cells) linked graph adjacency matrices:
code: # Aggregate Meuse observations onto a 6x6 spatial grid xbreaks <- seq(min(meuse$x), max(meuse$x), length.out = 7) ybreaks <- seq(min(meuse$y), max(meuse$y), length.out = 7)  meuse$cell_x  <- cut(meuse$x, xbreaks, include.lowest = TRUE, labels = FALSE) meuse$cell_y  <- cut(meuse$y, ybreaks, include.lowest = TRUE, labels = FALSE) meuse$cell_id <- (meuse$cell_y - 1) * 6 + meuse$cell_x  agg <- aggregate(log(zinc) ~ cell_id, data = meuse, FUN = mean) names(agg) <- c("cell_id", "y") cell_coords <- unique(meuse[, c("cell_id", "cell_x", "cell_y")]) agg <- merge(agg, cell_coords, by = "cell_id") agg <- agg[order(agg$cell_id), ]  # Construct Rook/Queen graph adjacency matrix n_cells <- nrow(agg) adj <- matrix(0, n_cells, n_cells) for (i in 1:n_cells) {   for (j in 1:n_cells) {     if (i != j) {       dx <- abs(agg$cell_x[i] - agg$cell_x[j])       dy <- abs(agg$cell_y[i] - agg$cell_y[j])       if (dx <= 1 && dy <= 1) adj[i, j] <- 1     }   } }  # Run 80% Areal Conformal Prediction out_areal <- scp_areal(y = agg$y, adjacency = adj, alpha = 0.20, decay = 1.0) print(out_areal) #> <spconform> areal conformal prediction #> Target coverage: 80.0% #> Number of prediction points: 21 #>    pred lower upper #> 1 5.966 5.148 6.785 #> 2 5.749 4.854 6.643 #> 3 5.981 5.145 6.817 #> 4 5.502 4.608 6.396 #> 5 6.495 4.576 8.415 #> 6 5.934 5.116 6.752 #> ... title: spconform 0.1.2
text: CRAN release: 2026-10-19 Resolved single-query coordinate vector bug scp_geostatistical(): 1D coordinate vectors passed s0 now properly coerced 1-row coordinate matrix matching training dimensions. Fixed graphics layout warning plot.spconform_diagnose(): replaced uneven matrix dimension recycling explicit layout matrix n_panels = 3, preventing duplicate panel drawing. Added strict input validations scp_geostatistical() scp_areal() guarding missing (NA) values coordinates responses. Added length validation na.rm support coverage_report() prevent silent vector recycling errors. Optimized default spatial bandwidth computation scp_geostatistical(): bandwidth now evaluated prior query loop rather recomputed per target location, yielding 50x speedup large query grids. Added representative spatial subsampling bandwidth evaluation calibration size N>1000N > 1000, keeping memory footprint strictly bounded. Added optional k_neighbors argument scp_geostatistical() localized kk-NN calibration, defaulting NULL complete backward compatibility. coverage_report() now evaluates reports strictly proper Winkler Interval Score (winkler_score) alongside empirical coverage mean interval width.

title: spconform 0.1.0
text: CRAN release: 2026-09-12 Initial release spconform CRAN. Implemented locally weighted split conformal prediction geostatistical (point-referenced) data (scp_geostatistical()). Implemented neighbourhood-weighted leave-one-conformal prediction areal (lattice) data (scp_areal()). Added kernel weighting utilities spatial spatio-temporal predictions (spatial_kernel_weights(), areal_neighbor_weights()). Implemented comprehensive spatial diagnostic tools multi-panel visualization (diagnose()). Included S3 methods printing, summarizing, plotting conformal prediction intervals (print(), summary(), plot(), coverage_report()).
